        SignedHeaders=content-type;host;x-amz-date, \

       &X-Amz-Date=20210313T011059Z&X-Amz-Expires=86400000&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host\
       &X-Amz-Signature=2c652c7bc9a3b75579db3d987d1e6dd056f0ac776c1e1d4ec91e2ce84e5ad3ae

        return "sqs", config.PORT_SQS

        python_cmd,

Based on my investigation, I've identified the root cause:

The Java AWS SDK sends S3 PUT requests using `STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD` (aws-chunked signed streaming). The request body received by LocalStack is the raw chunked-encoded body (with `chunk-size;chunk-signature=...` framing and `X-Amz-Decoded-Content-Length` header), but `check_content_md5()` in `localstack/services/s3/s3_listener.py` computes `md5(data)` over that raw chunked body — not the decoded payload. Since the `Content-MD5` header is computed by the SDK over the actual (decoded) payload, the MD5s never match → `BadDigest` error.

The fix needs to be in `localstack/services/s3/s3_listener.py`:
- `check_content_md5()` (line ~884) and `forward_request()` (line ~1180/1222): detect the streaming payload via the `STREAMING_HMAC_PAYLOAD` constant (defined at line 62 but currently unused), strip the chunk framing/signatures to recover the actual payload, and use that decoded data both for the MD5 validation and for forwarding to the backend (also updating Content-Length).

This is corroborated by the fact that `STREAMING_HMAC_PAYLOAD` is defined but unused in the codebase, and that `s3_listener.py` was last edited 2021-11-24 — right when this issue (filed 2021-11-22) was being fixed.
